llm.summary: Today is a two-event tape: the FOMC decision under Warsh (consensus hold, but the live debate is a December HIKE, not a cut) and after-the-bell earnings from Microsoft and Alphabet that will set the terms of the AI capex argument. Beneath the index, the dispersion is extreme — CNBC is explicitly calling the end of the 'Magnificent Seven' as a correlated bloc, and non-AI stocks are beating the S&P by six points this month even as Nvidia/AMD/Micron rally a third straight day on SK Hynix's blowout outlook. The flow data still contradicts the headline narrative: Energy (96), Staples (61), Health Care (56) and Utilities (48) are accelerating while Communication Services (-75) and Industrials (-50) bleed, Value leads Growth by 69 points, and the regime model has Stagflation (32.9, +13.8) and Reflation (31.4, +12.3) both rising while Goldilocks collapses. The AI complex is now financing itself reflexively — Nvidia putting $3B into Meta's offering that drew 5x demand, a $3.1B GPU-backed loan, Nvidia's supplier/customer circularity with AMD and Broadcom — exactly when 10-year yields are flirting with 5% and 'AI debt fears' are pushing money into Treasuries. The real economy is cleanly bifurcated: Visa beat and raised its dividend 16%, consumer confidence rose for the first time in four months, Royal Caribbean and Frontier raised — but housing is frozen with builders cutting prices at a record pace and Whirlpool guiding to a full-year loss. Power demand is the one place where the AI story and the real-asset flow story agree: Duke raised 2026 guidance, ERCOT sees a demand surge, gas plant construction costs are up 66%, and Constellation got a $5B DOE nuclear loan. Own the picks, shovels, electrons and cash flows; be skeptical of anything whose return depends on a lower discount rate.

market_thesis.short_term: Binary and headline-driven for 48 hours. A hold is fully priced; the risk is Warsh validating December hike optionality with inflation above 3% — that hits long-duration equities, gold (already struggling at $4,040) and crypto at once. The semis have momentum into MSFT/GOOGL prints (AMD +5.5%, ANET +5.5%, ALAB +10.5%, COHR +6.5% pre-market, Vertiv's beat-and-raise as the cleanest AI-capex tell), so the near-term path of least resistance for AI hardware is up — but the same prints are the single biggest downside catalyst if capex guidance comes with depreciation and funding caveats. Expect Value>Growth and Energy/Staples/Health Care leadership to persist regardless of the index level.
market_thesis.medium_term: Stagflation-lite remains the base case into H1 2027: inflation sticky above 3%, oil firm on Middle East supply risk (drone attack on a UAE nuclear plant, Iranian gas shortage), jobs softening, and an AI capex cycle that is itself inflationary for power, copper, turbines, labour and credit. That mix compresses multiples for unprofitable or narrative growth while rewarding pricing power, contracted cash flow and real assets. The AI trade bifurcates further: compute, memory, networking, cooling, grid and nuclear keep compounding on contracted demand; AI-adjacent software with unproven agent monetisation de-rates. Watch financing structure as the key fragility — equity issuance, GPU-collateralised loans and private credit are now the marginal funders of the buildout, and that is reflexive to rates.
market_thesis.long_term: The electricity-and-compute supercycle is the durable structural trade: ERCOT demand surging into the 2030s, IRENA raising its 2035 target to 18.4TW, pipeline owners racing to add capacity, the US military wanting reactors to survive 90 days off-grid, and AI data centres being sited at retired nuclear plants. That implies a decade of grid, gas, nuclear, copper and semicap spend with policy backing. Simultaneously, housing undersupply plus frozen affordability reshapes a generation's consumption toward experiences, value retail and delayed household formation. Health care — metabolic health, continuous monitoring, longevity — takes rising share of discretionary spend as populations age. And sovereign/retail capital is globalising fast (Jio's record IPO +21% on debut, Indian investors buying Nvidia and SpaceX through local apps), which widens the funding pool for the same handful of AI assets.

short_term: Consumers are spending but trading down: Visa's beat plus Coca-Cola's beat alongside a 'resilient with signs of strain' read means volume is holding while value-seeking intensifies — Dollar General, Dollar Tree and Target attention is elevated for a reason.

Households are abandoning the housing ladder rather than stretching for it: mortgage rates fell two straight weeks yet more borrowers are reaching for riskier loan structures, and builders are slashing prices at a record pace — buyers are waiting, not bidding.

Discretionary dollars are flowing to experiences over goods: Royal Caribbean raised guidance, Frontier posted record Q3 revenue up 53% despite high fuel, while Whirlpool guides to a full-year loss on appliance demand.

Retail investors are rotating away from crypto toward equities and global access: Robinhood's crypto revenue fell 55% and ARPU missed even with record trading volumes, while Indian retail rushes into Nvidia, SpaceX and Apple via new US-access apps.

Enterprises are getting disciplined about AI token spend — Amazon's internal 'anti-tokenmaxxing' memo telling engineers to be pickier is the first visible sign that inference consumption is being budgeted, not assumed.

Public attention is migrating from AI models to AI agents (+139% vs 28-day, queries about agents accessing bank accounts), which means the monetisation question becomes mainstream and therefore testable.
long_term: Energy is becoming a household-level anxiety and a status-differentiated good: rising 'electricity bill' search intent (+18.6%) alongside data-centre-driven demand means consumers will eventually notice they are competing with compute for electrons — a political and regulatory flashpoint.

Security of all kinds — cyber, energy, supply chain — is being repriced as a necessity rather than an overhead: a cyberattack forced Boston Scientific to cut guidance, the FEC system went offline days before midterms, and the US military is designing for grid independence.

Delayed household formation and 'buy, borrow and die' wealth strategies ($5T market) entrench a bifurcated consumer: asset owners compound, wage earners optimise for convenience and value, and the middle thins out.

Knowledge and productivity work is being restructured around agents rather than seats, which over years changes how software is priced — consumption and outcome pricing replaces per-user subscriptions.
Health moves from episodic treatment to continuous measurement: continuous glucose monitoring, diagnostics and metabolic management become default consumer infrastructure, not medical exceptions.

Capital markets are globalising retail access (Jio IPO, US-stock apps in India), deepening the pool of marginal buyers for a narrow set of global mega-cap AI assets — more liquidity on the way up, more correlation on the way down.
